evidence_policy.documented: Upstream material names or exercises the weakness; not itself verification.
evidence_policy.source-reviewed: Entry point, controls, data flow and root cause inspected at the exact source pin; runtime not implied.
evidence_policy.reproduced: An isolated request/exploit oracle was executed successfully against this exact pin with environment and result recorded.

evaluation.deduplication: One record per root cause. Match the mechanism and primary region or a decisive related control (for example admin_param at admin_controller.rb:76 for RAILSGOAT-003). CWE or nearby line alone is insufficient. Related locations are evidence, not independent positives; ambiguous matches need manual adjudication.
known_leakage: Upstream application source and templates contain answer-bearing vulnerability comments and tutorial code.
The withhold list alone is not a blinded export. A reviewed transformation with a reversible line map is required before calling an evaluation blind.
Public training repositories can appear in model training data even after annotation stripping.

manifest.upstream_test_caveat: RAILSGOAT_MAINTAINER makes verifying_fixed? return false (spec/support/capybara_shared.rb:11-35); vulnerability before hooks skip. Green upstream maintainer CI cannot establish exploit reproduction.
exclusions: No claim of exhaustive vulnerability coverage or safe/unvulnerable regions.
Dependencies/SCA, deployment configuration and tutorial-only exercises are not part of this pilot.
No repaired snapshots, verified negatives or blinded scanner export are included.

findings.title: Employee information lookup is not scoped to the signed-in user
findings.label: vulnerable
findings.root_cause: WorkInfoController#index selects the requested user globally and rejects only missing/admin targets; it never requires the target to equal current_user.
preconditions: Authenticated ordinary user who passes ApplicationController#has_info
Another non-admin user exists with a work_info record
Attacker can choose the nested user_id route parameter
findings.security_invariant: An ordinary employee may read only their own employee information.
flow: User.find_by loads that identity independently of current_user.
The view renders the selected user's income, bonus, SSN and date of birth.

evidence.upstream_spec_assessment: Training-mode assertion expects another user's information NOT to be visible. The before hook at lines 8–10 skips the scenario when RAILSGOAT_MAINTAINER is set. Not executed here.

runtime.reason: Ruby, Bundler and Docker are not installed in the annotation workspace; no Rails request or exploit was executed.
runtime.expected_vulnerable_observation: With distinct ordinary users A and B, a request authenticated as A for B's work_info returns B's record rather than denying access.

limitations: Admin targets are explicitly rejected; this record covers other non-admin employees.
JavaScript masks SSN in the DOM after delivery; masking does not authorize or remove sensitive data from the response.

findings.title: Signup accepts the privileged admin attribute
findings.label: vulnerable
findings.root_cause: UsersController#user_params marks every submitted user attribute permitted, and #create passes the result to User.new, including the persisted admin flag.
preconditions: Signup is enabled and unauthenticated create is reachable
Provide a new valid email and a password with matching confirmation satisfying model validation
findings.security_invariant: Public signup must not allow the registrant to choose an administrative role.
flow: The create action is excluded from the authenticated filter.
params.require(:user).permit! accepts the attacker-supplied admin field.
User.new and save persist admin on the new account and establish its session.

evidence.upstream_spec_assessment: The upstream scenario submits admin during signup and asserts the resulting account is NOT admin; it is a repair-oriented assertion, skipped in maintainer mode (lines 7–9). Not executed here.

runtime.reason: Ruby, Bundler and Docker are not installed in the annotation workspace; no Rails request or exploit was executed.
runtime.expected_vulnerable_observation: A valid signup containing admin=true creates an account whose reloaded admin attribute is true.

limitations: Separate self-service update permitting admin at users_controller.rb:55 is a different assignment boundary, intentionally not included in this label.
Do not count every writable field as a separate root cause.

findings.title: Route parameter disables the administrative authorization filter
findings.label: vulnerable
findings.root_cause: AdminController applies its administrative callback only when admin_param is true; admin_param returns false for attacker-selected admin_id equal to the string 1.
findings.security_invariant: Every administrative action must authorize the current authenticated user regardless of URL identifiers.
flow: The admin resource exposes nested routes with admin_id.
The callback condition depends on that route parameter rather than the authenticated principal.
For admin_id=1, the administrative filter is skipped and get_all_users loads every user.

evidence.upstream_spec_assessment: The upstream scenario requests /admin/1/dashboard and expects a redirect away. It documents the same callback bypass but does not assert the stronger get_all_users data exposure. The before hook skips it in maintainer mode. Not executed here.

runtime.reason: Ruby, Bundler and Docker are not installed in the annotation workspace; no Rails request or exploit was executed.
runtime.expected_vulnerable_observation: A non-admin request to /admin/1/get_all_users reaches the action and returns the full user list.

limitations: The explicitly excepted get_user action is a separate missing-check boundary and is not counted here.
The selected read-only entry point demonstrates the same callback root cause without deleting records.

findings.title: Account update interpolates the request identity into SQL
findings.label: vulnerable
findings.root_cause: UsersController#update constructs the where condition by interpolating params[:user][:id] inside a quoted SQL string without binding or escaping it.
findings.entry_point: PUT or PATCH /users/:id with nested user[id]
preconditions: Request includes a user object and a syntactically valid database-specific SQL fragment in user[id]
Any update attributes satisfy relevant model validations
findings.security_invariant: Request identity values must be treated as SQL data and must not alter predicate structure.
flow: The action consumes nested user[id], not the route id, as query text.
String interpolation constructs the SQL predicate supplied to User.where.
The first matching row is subsequently updated with the supplied account attributes.

evidence.upstream_spec_assessment: The spec mutates a hidden identity field with SQL syntax and checks that an administrator email was NOT changed. It is skipped in maintainer mode. Its exact historical payload is adapter/query-shape dependent and has not been verified against this Rails 8 pin.

runtime.reason: Ruby, Bundler and Docker are not installed in the annotation workspace; no Rails request or exploit was executed.
runtime.expected_vulnerable_observation: A carefully chosen predicate-changing identity fragment changes the selected row(s); an explicit oracle must assert a chosen fixture's persistent state, not merely an HTTP error or any test failure.

limitations: The manifest selects the upstream SQLite test configuration; some other RailsGoat SQL demonstrations require MySQL. No claim is made that this spec's exact payload works on every adapter.
Missing ownership authorization at the same action is a distinct root cause. A report describing only unscoped selection should not be matched to this SQL injection label.

findings.title: Backup command embeds an uploaded filename in shell command text
findings.label: vulnerable
findings.root_cause: Benefits.make_backup interpolates file.original_filename, directly and via full_file_name, into a single-string system call without shell escaping or argument separation.
preconditions: Multipart filename retains shell metacharacters and ends in an allowed extension (.pdf, .doc, .docx, .jpg, .jpeg or .png)
Upload is no larger than 10 MiB and the target data directory is writable
benefits[backup] is the literal string true; saved file exists; shell/cp are available
findings.security_invariant: Uploaded filenames must remain opaque data and must not become shell syntax.
flow: upload obtains the uploaded file and validates only extension and size.
Benefits.save constructs a path from original_filename, writes the file and calls make_backup when backup == true as a string.
make_backup embeds the filename in a shell-interpreted system command.

evidence.upstream_spec_assessment: STALE ORACLE: the historical filename at line 21 has no allowed extension, so current upload validation rejects it before Benefits.save. Its .new_benefits form selector and Start Upload button selector are stale as well (the current form has explicit class needs-validation and the button is Upload File). Its destructive cleanup payload must not be reused. A green training assertion would not establish that the shell vulnerability is absent. It is also skipped in maintainer mode.

runtime.reason: Ruby, Bundler and Docker are not installed in the annotation workspace; no Rails request or exploit was executed.
runtime.expected_vulnerable_observation: In an isolated disposable runtime, an allowed-extension filename containing a harmless marker-producing shell fragment causes that marker to be created only when backup=true. Use a negative control with backup=false and do not run the upstream destructive payload.

limitations: No upload parsing, command execution or Rails runtime was exercised; this is source-reviewed evidence only.
An updated non-destructive behavioral oracle is still required, including confirmation that Rack preserves the selected filename characters.
Filename/path traversal during the write is a separate unannotated root cause.

findings.title: Download accepts an unconstrained filesystem path
findings.label: vulnerable
findings.root_cause: BenefitFormsController#download constructs an object from request-controlled type and name and passes it to send_file without restricting the path to approved benefit files.
preconditions: Choose type=File and an existing file readable by the application process
send_file accepts the resulting File object/path representation on the pinned Rails runtime
findings.security_invariant: Benefit downloads must be restricted to authorized files in the intended download directory.
flow: params[:name] supplies the path and params[:type] selects the class.
With type=File, File.new opens the requested path without a benefit-directory allowlist.
send_file attempts to return the opened file to the requester.

evidence.upstream_spec_assessment: The upstream scenario replaces the download name with config/database.yml and expects no successful download. Its first(".widget-body a") selector is stale: the current benefit page has no .widget-body element, so this UI scenario cannot reach the download. It is skipped in maintainer mode. Not executed here.

runtime.reason: Ruby, Bundler and Docker are not installed in the annotation workspace; no Rails request or exploit was executed.
runtime.expected_vulnerable_observation: An authenticated direct download request for a benign fixture outside the benefit directory returns the fixture bytes rather than rejecting the path.

limitations: CWE-73 describes externally controlled file paths without assuming a ../ traversal payload.
Ruby object coercion at send_file must be verified before promoting this label to reproduced; exceptions cause redirect in the rescue block.
Attacker-controlled constantize also warrants separate review; no arbitrary code execution claim is made from constantize alone.
